response_text:
**Summary**

The video explains that our immune system is constantly surveilling and destroying rogue cells before they can develop into cancer—most of these events go unnoticed. Cancer arises when a cell’s DNA becomes corrupted and the cell begins to proliferate uncontrollably, ignoring the cooperative rules that keep a multicellular organism healthy. Because every tissue type can give rise to cancer, there are hundreds of distinct cancers that vary in growth rate, aggressiveness, and treatability.

The narrative frames cancer as a breakdown of the evolutionary shift from solitary, competitive cells to cooperative, specialized cells that make up multicellular organisms. In a healthy body, the collective’s welfare outweighs the interests of any single cell; cancer cells reject this collective responsibility, reverting to a selfish, “self‑ish” mode that threatens the organism. The immune system’s continual “clean‑up” work is what prevents most potential cancers from ever becoming disease.
